answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting jobs, whether it sells sable pelts, dune maps, or crystal samples. The bond stays locked even if the identity leaves early, so creating 1,000 fake sellers ties up $100,000 for a month. Splitting one operator into many accounts therefore consumes capital in direct proportion to the number of identities, making a sybil swarm costly to maintain.
